title: Ensuring Social Media Platforms' Rules of Engagement for Online Advertisements are In Line with Local Regulations
what_it_is: Ensuring Social Media Platforms' Rules of Engagement for Online Advertisements are In Line with Local Regulations

sections.label: Advertising rules and social media
sections.summary: The SCAP covers all advertisements, ASAS reviews complaints and can require amendments, and designated social media services must minimise harmful content exposure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The SCAP applies to all advertisements for any goods and services appearing in any form or any media, including on social media services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: It stipulates that all advertisements should be legal, decent, honest and truthful.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: ASAS’ Guidelines on Interactive Marketing Communication and Social Media further set out the standards of ethical conduct that are to be adopted by marketers, advertising agencies or media that are involved in social media marketing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: ASAS adopts a complaints-based approach in reviewing potential advertising breaches when reported to them and can get advertisers to amend or withdraw advertisements that are deemed to have breached the Guidelines or SCAP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: Designated social media services with significant reach or impact are also required under the Code of Practice for Online Safety issued by the Infocomm Media Development Authority to minimise users’ exposure to harmful content.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
sentences.text: The designated social media services are Facebook, HardwareZone, Instagram, TikTok, X and YouTube.

sections.label: False claims unfair trade practice
sections.summary: Making a false or misleading claim about products and services may constitute an unfair trade practice under the CPFTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Sometimes, they are reputational costs because of the publicity given to the advertisement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Therefore, making a false or misleading claim about products and services may also constitute an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act, or CPFTA.

sections.label: Contempt for breaching injunction
sections.summary: If a company under injunction does not comply, CCCS can take the advertiser to court for contempt, a criminal offence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: If a company under injunction does not comply with the injunction order, CCCS can take the advertiser to court for contempt of court, which is a criminal offence that could result in a fine or imprisonment.
